Subject: Initial: residency & snapshots — high-level questions

Neha,

Thanks again for the call this morning. A few follow-ups from Acme's side as we review the DPA redlines:

1) Snapshots/backups: we need clarity on whether scheduled snapshots (daily/weekly) can be configured to be stored in the customer-selected region only, including immutable backups created for HA. Our security team is concerned about cross-region replication for backups that may contain PHI.

2) Deletion confirmation: when a user requests account deletion, what exact operational steps does Redwood take to ensure backups and ephemeral caches are removed? We need an auditable confirmation chain (who/when/where).

3) Escrow / legal hold: if Acme issues a legal hold after deletion, do you maintain a separate hold state, and how is that reconciled with erase commitments?

I've attached a small CSV we pulled from our inventories to illustrate the retention classes we're dealing with. Can your ops and legal teams advise concrete, redlineable language for these three areas?

Appreciate a prioritized response — our procurement timeline is tight.

Regards,
Lena Ortiz
Director, Data Security
Acme Health

Lena — thanks for laying this out and for the CSV; useful context. Quick answers up front, then proposed next steps + what we'll put in redline language: 

1) Snapshots/backups: yes — we can support region-locked scheduled snapshots. There are two modes we should propose in the DPA:
   - Region-locked: backups and snapshots are written only to the customer-selected region(s) and no cross-region replication is enabled unless explicitly requested.
   - HA replication with control plane visibility: if you require automatic cross-region HA replication, Redwood will document where replicas are stored and provide additional contractual safeguards (encryption keys, access controls, and an explicit carve-out in the DPA).

2) Deletion confirmation: operationally we run a staged sweep — (a) remove active tenant data, (b) mark snapshots/tombstones for purge and queue for secure delete, (c) remove keys (for BYOK cases) and schedule physical/logical purge. We can provide an erase report (CSV) that includes timestamps and operator IDs.

3) Legal hold: we treat legal holds as a separate retention override. If a hold is issued after deletion request, we can suspend purge and track the hold lifecycle; we propose adding a notification window and a maximum hold duration clause to keep expectations explicit.

Proposed next steps:
- Jonas / Marissa to draft redline language for the three areas and attach a proposed DPA snippet.
- We'll produce an "erase confirmation" template and an example report for your review.
- If helpful, we can run a short runbook walk-through with your security ops team next week.

Looping in Jonas and Marissa to draft the redlines.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--

Hi Lena / Neha — attaching our draft redline language and a short ops playbook excerpt for the snapshot sweep. Key callouts inline: 

- Snapshots: propose the DPA add a new subsection: "Snapshot and Backup Residency" that states: "Redwood will, by default, store scheduled snapshots in the customer-selected region(s). Cross-region replication for backups will only occur where Customer has provided written authorization; such replication will be limited to regions specified by Customer."

- Purge flow: proposed language to guarantee a two-stage purge window (30 days tombstone, then secure delete) for standard customers, with the option to shorten via SOW for regulated customers. We explicitly call out logs and erase-report delivery.

- Legal hold: propose a clause that legal holds suspend purge and that Redwood will provide a written acknowledgement within 3 business days, and will maintain a hold audit log. Maximum hold default of 12 months unless extended by mutual written agreement.

Attachments in this message: proposed_dpa_redline_v2.docx; erase_flow_diagram.png.

If you want stricter timelines (e.g., immediate wipe of backups rather than staggered tombstone window), we can table that as a special carve-out and outline operational and cost implications.

-Jonas

Lena — quick ops-level reply and a sample erase confirmation attached inline below.

Operational feasibility: we can implement a tenant-level hard block on cross-region replication for backups flagged as "PHI-sensitive." That will prevent automated replication unless Acme requests an explicit SOW to lift the block. The engineering changes are straightforward: an additional region flag on snapshot policies and an enforcement gate in the replication controller. There is a small runbook and testing window (~2-3 weeks) to roll to production for a first-party tenant.

7-day tombstone for PHI: feasible. The difference is more on monitoring and storage churn. We'll propose two options in the SOW appendix: (A) 7-day tombstone + immediate secure delete, (B) 30-day tombstone as default. I'll attach a sample erase confirmation CSV with columns: record_id, data_type, deletion_requested_at, deletion_completed_at, deletion_operator, storage_region, retention_class, legal_hold_flag.
